name: Adaptability
definition: A decision table for assessing the adaptability of AI systems.

x_org.owasp#aivss:CM:0.1.0.name: Continuous Monitoring
x_org.owasp#aivss:CM:0.1.0.definition: Degree to which the system is continuously monitored for threats, anomalies, and performance degradation.

values.name: Real-Time Automation
values.definition: Real-time monitoring with automated response to detected threats, including dynamic model adaptation and rollback capabilities.

values.name: Comprehensive Monitoring
values.definition: Comprehensive monitoring of system inputs, outputs, and internal states, with anomaly detection algorithms and automated alerts for suspicious activity.

values.name: Basic Monitoring
values.definition: Basic monitoring in place, but limited analysis and no automated alerts.

values.name: None
values.definition: No monitoring for adversarial attacks, anomalies, or performance degradation.

x_org.owasp#aivss:RE:0.1.0.name: Retraining Capabilities
x_org.owasp#aivss:RE:0.1.0.definition: Degree to which the system supports retraining and adaptation to new data or conditions.

values.name: Continuous Automated Retraining
values.definition: Continuous and automated retraining triggered by performance degradation, concept drift, or new data, with minimal human intervention.

values.name: Automated Pipeline
values.definition: Automated retraining pipeline in place, allowing for regular updates with new data and model improvements.

values.name: Manual Retraining
values.definition: Manual retraining possible, but infrequent and time-consuming, with limited automation.

values.name: None
values.definition: No capability to retrain the model, or retraining requires significant manual effort and downtime.

x_org.owasp#aivss:TI:0.1.0.name: Threat Intelligence Integration
x_org.owasp#aivss:TI:0.1.0.definition: Degree to which threat intelligence is integrated into security operations and risk mitigation.

values.name: Proactive Hunting
values.definition: Proactive threat hunting based on threat intelligence, with automated analysis and correlation of threat data to identify and mitigate risks before impact.

values.name: Integrated Feeds
values.definition: Threat intelligence feeds integrated into security monitoring and response systems, providing automated alerts and updates on emerging threats.

values.name: Basic Use
values.definition: Basic threat intelligence used, but not systematically integrated into security operations.

values.name: None
values.definition: No integration with threat intelligence feeds or other sources of security information.

x_org.owasp#aivss:AT:0.1.0.name: Adversarial Training
x_org.owasp#aivss:AT:0.1.0.definition: Degree to which adversarial training is used to improve model robustness.

values.name: Continuous Adversarial Training
values.definition: Continuous adversarial training with evolving attack techniques, incorporating new attacks as they are discovered, and using formal verification methods to ensure robustness.

values.name: Robust Adversarial Training
values.definition: Robust adversarial training against a wide range of attacks with larger perturbation budgets, using multiple techniques.

values.name: Basic Adversarial Training
values.definition: Basic adversarial training with a limited set of attack types and small perturbation budgets.

values.name: None
values.definition: No adversarial training used during model development.

x_org.owasp#aivss:AD:0.1.0.name: Adaptability
x_org.owasp#aivss:AD:0.1.0.definition: A decision point for assessing the adaptability of AI models.

values.name: None
values.definition: No known vulnerability or a formally proven resistance to the specific threat.

values.name: Low
values.definition: Low vulnerability with strong mitigation in place, but some minor weaknesses may still exist.

values.name: Medium
values.definition: Moderate vulnerability with some mitigation, but significant weaknesses remain.

values.name: High
values.definition: Severe vulnerability with little to no mitigation in place.
